gaps.sentence: 'Let's walk to the launch instead of driving,' he said. He ___ to the launch instead of driving.
gaps.explanation: 'Suggest' takes a gerund, never a to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Shall I close the window?' he asked. He asked ___ close the window.
gaps.explanation: Shall I...? (offering) becomes if/whether he should... in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I had already eaten,' she said. She said she ___ already eaten.
gaps.explanation: The past perfect cannot backshift further; it remains had + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: 'When does the library open?' she asked. She asked ___ the library opened.
gaps.explanation: The original question word 'when' is kept in the reported clause.
